page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 15.0 GB, which equates to 1.88 GB of RAM per core. It includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a mix of average and weak performance. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests falls into the average category, as do memory bandwidth tests and static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the bottom 10% and single-threaded compression tasks showing weak results. Software compilation with Clang and image processing benchmarks maintain average performance tiers, while LLM inference tasks on larger models are poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3.2xlarge offers a legacy hardware profile with dedicated compute resources and bundled local NVMe SSD storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring predictable CPU allocation without the premium of newer generation architectures. Given its balanced multi-core capabilities and local storage, it is suited for workloads such as static web serving, basic database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation.
